item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine has deployed naval drones to strike Russian warships in Libya’s Benghazi port, claiming lawful self-defence. Russia has violated Finnish airspace with a helicopter and Polish airspace with an unmanned aerial vehicle. NATO’s chief has pledged defence against a Russian space threat after reports of a planned nuclear satellite. MI5 has warned UK firms supplying Ukraine of sabotage risk. The UN Security Council warned that winter attacks on Ukraine’s power grid and Black Sea shipping threaten lives and global food supplies, and 75,767 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed a Hamas political official, his wife and children, a senior education official and seven others, and separately eliminated a Hamas-appointed minister. Israel has threatened to displace one million Palestinians in Gaza unless Hamas disarms, and a report says Israel officially sanctions torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions. Shin Bet has freed an Arab Israeli who was held for alleged election tampering. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Hezbollah chief again demanded Lebanon release five detained operatives while rejecting any post-UNIFIL force outside U.N. authority, and he reiterated that Iran works for Hezbollah. Israeli warplanes intensified low-altitude flights over southern Lebanon and the Nabatieh region and Israel opposed French troop deployment in south Lebanon, warning it would grant Hezbollah freedom of movement. Israeli airstrikes hit the town of Hadatha and Israeli forces shelled, demolished and swept southern Lebanon, while a Jordanian sailor’s body was recovered near the UAE coast after a tanker attack. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthis launched retaliatory strikes on two Saudi ports on the Red Sea and hit Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery, producing a plume of black smoke visible from space, while also targeting a financial district in Riyadh. Saudi forces intercepted drones and missiles over the Red Sea and western Yemen in response to the attacks. The intensified Houthi operations have raised concerns about worsening the humanitarian crisis at Hodeidah port. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
ISIL has continued to target Syrian security forces, killing two internal security members in a suicide attack in Hasakah and injuring several others, while another suicide bombing in Tartous wounded a security officer and killed a gunman. The Syrian government is considering a law to grant nationality to children of foreign fighters, reflecting concerns about the legacy of extremist participation. Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Jordan have issued condemnations of attacks on Syrian security facilities, indicating regional diplomatic responses. Syrian authorities seized Iranian weapons destined for Lebanon, showing ongoing arms interdiction efforts. 2,732 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Baghdad is deploying troops to secure Kurdistan borders after the top court authorized a military presence and takeover of border posts and oil fields, while the prime minister seeks greater authority over the Kurdish region and the defense ministry orders nationwide troop deployment and closure of oil smuggling routes. Iraqi drone strikes have destroyed a militant vehicle in Anbar province and Hezbollah fighters have been transferred onto Popular Mobilization Forces payroll. Germany arrested an Iraqi duo suspected of plotting attacks on synagogues, and an Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life imprisonment for IS group membership. The conflict recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
Drone strikes hit a United Nations building and residential areas in Khartoum, killing four people and threatening humanitarian operations, while RSF forces assaulted aid offices in Nyala and a shelter in West Kordofan, causing civilian casualties. RSF counterintelligence chief, a commander and a group defected to the Sudanese army in Khartoum, indicating shifting loyalties. RSF-aligned forces intensified drone attacks in Blue Nile state, killing 19 civilians and displacing thousands as they approached Ed Damazin. Ethiopia offered to host inclusive Sudan peace talks and propose a national unity government, but Sudan rejected the offer, questioning Ethiopia's neutrality, and the conflict produced 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
Armed clashes and intercommunal violence persist in South Sudan, with rebel and SPLA-IO forces attacking civilians in Tonj East, Warrap State and Greater Pibor, while worshippers were attacked in Gorom refugee camp and a teen was killed for refusing an arranged marriage. UNMISS is supporting deterrence efforts in Tonj East and calling for stronger civilian protection during a visit to Unity, and the Gender Ministry has raised concerns about violence against women and children ahead of a 16 Days campaign. President Kiir told an Oil and Power conference that partnerships, not speeches, must change lives, after travelling to Ethiopia and holding investment talks with Saudi Arabia in Riyadh. A US senator warned that Uganda is playing a destabilising role, the Crisis Group urged African intervention, and the UNDP resident representative issued a message of solidarity. There were 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Somali federal forces and U.S. airstrikes have recently killed dozens of al-Shabaab militants in Lower Shabelle, while Turkish-made missiles were identified in a deadly Somalia airstrike. The Somali parliament speaker has accused Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda of colluding with al-Shabaab, and the president has blamed the UAE for financing armed groups. The United States has reversed its funding for international military support to Somalia. Al-Shabaab is reported to be collaborating with Houthi forces, raising concerns for global trade. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Militant groups in Nigeria's Niger state carried out a reprisal attack that killed at least 30 civilians and later deployed more tactical teams to the area, while separate assaults killed 11 soldiers in the southeast, 16 near the Malian border and 25 in another strike. Fulani communities suffered mass killings of at least 64 people, and a Saudi national was kidnapped by suspected Islamic State militants in Niger. Insurgents have begun using off-the-shelf drones, and rebels in Mali claim Ukrainian officers are training them on drone tactics, while a Russian envoy reports over 300 Russian soldiers killed in Mali. The Sahel jihadist insurgency caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
M23 rebels have withdrawn from near Bunia after heavy clashes but opened a new front near the Uganda border and are advancing on Uvira city. WHO evacuated its Ebola response team from an Ituri hospital after they were trapped by fighting, and the Ebola death rate is now near 50%. A Congolese military aircraft went missing after rebels claimed to have shot it down, leading to the capture of a South African mercenary. The conflict has displaced 8.2 million people and caused 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Central African Republic: the situation
item.description:

The UN Security Council renewed the MINUSCA mandate to 2027, lowered the troop ceiling to 12,000 and ordered a gradual drawdown of peacekeepers while extending the mission. Saudi backing now funds a second year of a Sahel counter-terrorism programme centred on Chad, and tensions have risen between Chad and Niger after a prison break in Chad that caused two inmate deaths and 30 escapes. Wagner’s gold interests continue to block peace efforts, and 246 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
